source: Round-24 drift-arbiter run on T-05 i18n spec_gap. First ever `amend_design` verdict in the wild — prior arbiter cases were all `amend_task`. Triggered by cold-reader veto (HIGH/scope_4 + HIGH/scope_3) on the silent-resolution pattern: T-05's task body authorized two deferrals (chips deferred to T-20, Spanish-as-English stubs) but the cited §D6 didn't authorize either, so cold-reader correctly flagged both as silent producer resolutions.

spec_gap.gap_description: T-05's task body authorizes two deferrals: (a) chip-specific keys (`incidents.chips.*`) deferred to T-20, blocked on DQ-5; (b) Spanish translations as English-value stubs since strict JSON disallows the design's `// TODO i18n-es` marker. Both deferrals are in the task body but NOT in the cited design §D6. Cold-reader correctly flagged both as silent producer resolutions (HIGH/scope_4 for chip omission vs §D6's enumerated subtree; HIGH/scope_3 for silent ambiguity-resolution on Spanish stubs vs NFR-5). Root cause: task-body caveats are invisible to the cold-reader by design (cold-reader only sees cited spec/design + diff). The harness needs the cited design to authorize what the task body assumes — otherwise every task with a 'do X except Y' caveat will get cold-reader vetoed.
spec_gap.suggested_amendment: Amend §D6 (in `02-design.md`) to (1) add a 'Deferrals' subsection explicitly deferring `incidents.chips.*` to T-20 (gated on DQ-5 resolution); (2) add a §D6.1 'Spanish-stub convention' subsection acknowledging that JSON file format precludes inline TODO comments and authorizing English-value stubs in `es/common.json` for v1, with the stub→translation work happening in a dedicated post-foundation task. Both amendments preserve every other §D6 claim. Add corresponding §D11 changelog entry citing the round-24 spec_gap from T-05.

actual_baseline.notes: Arbiter chose a single contiguous insertion (one Deferrals note covering both deferrals) over the suggested two-subsection amendment, citing minimal-blast-radius. Recognized 'two changes in one amendment' is permitted because both are within §D6 (not across artifacts). Also surfaced a methodology-level observation (out of scope for this arbitration): task-body caveats are invisible to cold-reader; either builders need to require cited-artifact authorization for deferrals OR the cold-reader input needs visibility into task notes. Surfaces the same gap pattern as round-19's T-01 case but on a different axis.

notes: Critical milestone: first `amend_design` case in any eval suite. Prior arbiter cases all hit `amend_task` because foundation tasks (especially T-01) needed verify-line tweaks. Validates that the arbiter's verdict-selection logic actually picks the right artifact when the gap lives in design rather than task. Also captures a real instance of the methodology gap the arbiter named in `actual_baseline.notes` — task-body caveats vs cold-reader scope. That gap is now logged as PR-B/methodology material; not fixed in this PR. Re-cold-reading T-05 against amended §D6 produced clean approve, confirming the loop closes.
